utterances.text: We know that they are dead if relevant documents exist. We don't know whether they are dead if they are noted as missing by ICRC. And some notions have been mixed here. I think that you insist on something that Dr. Tabeau has not written. She says that she has difficulties with all sources of information, but she says such and such sources are relevant. I don't have them. The next difficulty is that some cases of death are such that persons may be dead or may have survived. But that's not a relevant source. Dr. Tabeau also gives the sources of the information on the basis of which she draws such a conclusion, so perhaps if would be good to show the sources of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: You said: "We know that they are dead if relevant documents exist." But if you've exhumed someone's remains from the ground, they've been DNA identified, we know they are dead. We don't need additional documents; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We know that they are dead but we don't know where and when they were killed. And Dr. Tabeau is working on Tomasica noting dates and places of death or when and where a person went missing. I do not contest that the DNA shows where a person was found, in which grave, and that this person was identified, and this is scientific. But it is not scientific proof nor can it be established where and when and under what conditions this person lost his or her life.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Radovanovic, I put it to you that what you've done here is you've pulled this quotation out of context in a way that misrepresents the point Dr. Tabeau is making in her article. You're taking a quotation that relates to sources that might potentially report someone incorrectly as being dead who could be alive, and it doesn't apply to this situation; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are wrong. The whole quotation saying what the relevant sources for establishing death are, a relevant source cannot be misleading as to whether someone has been found to be dead or alive. She says that it has to be a source from the registry of deaths or a court decision. And all this that precedes refers to the sources which Dr. Tabeau is using. And there are problems with that. Because she says that only a few sources can be taken as safe and sound here, and she does not use any of those in Tomasica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Radovanovic, what is put to you is that Dr. Tabeau writes about a problem which may arise if there still can be uncertainty about whether someone has died, yes or no, and for that situation, she describes what she considers to be reliable sources. What Mr. File puts to you is that when such uncertainty does not exist because the body has been exhumed and DNA-identified, that what Dr. Tabeau writes here is for such situations irrelevant. That is what is put to you, and do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think I have understood you quite well. If a body is exhumed and identified, I do not dispute that this person is dead. I only say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- so I'm not disputing the death.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for that situation, whether or not death certificates or court decisions are there is irrelevant for establishing whether someone is dead or alive.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is unimportant in that situation. But not as regards Tomasica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. File. I -- and one short additional question. Have dead bodies been found in Tomasica where identification through DNA took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 184 are listed by Dr. Tabeau that she received the DNA information from the prosecutor's office of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Unless I'm mistaken. So if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't -- I didn't ask you all that. I just asked whether in Tomasica such cases exist. That is, body exhumed --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of the dead?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Body exhumed, DNA-identified, do such cases exist in Tomasica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Did you say 184 or 384?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 184. I'm not sure if it is 184 or 194. That was received from the prosecutor's office of Bosnia-Herzegovina. ICMP said something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at your report again.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: D1484 MFI, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: This time we're going to look at page 22 of the English and page 29 of the B/C/S. This will be paragraph 67. So I'm referring to the part of the paragraph that you put in bold typeface, where you say: "... no table indicates the source of the data on the basis of which it was made."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So if we could switch to look at the Ewa Tabeau Tomasica report, P7449, please. We're going to start at English page 15, B/C/S page 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm just going to take you through a couple of examples when this comes up. If you look at Table 7, the title of that table is: "Place of disappearance in the ICMP records of the Tomasica identified." And then if you go down to Table 8, you see: "Place of disappearance in the ICRC records of the Tomasica identified." And then table 9 says: "15 most frequent places of disappearance according to ICRC and KNP records." Just to give you one last slightly different example, if we could go to English page 18 and B/C/S page 22, Table 12, you see the title: "Time of disappearance in ICMP records of the Tomasica identified." And then in case we missed what's written in the title, if we could just go to English page 19 and B/C/S page 23, the first paragraph of text reiterates: "The source for Table 12 was the ICMP ..." So how can you say that no table indicates the source of the data on the basis of which it was made when all have you to do is read the title of the table or the text of the document?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are not right. This is technically not right, and there are two ICMP reports, one is from May and the other is from June. There are two books of lists of Prijedor victims, one is from 2008 and the other one is from 2002, I think. And then what else. ICRC. There is ICRC where Dr. Tabeau says for the source in 2009 which sources she used and then she tells us next, I was working everything in accordance data from 2005. So what would have been scientifically acceptable, what one does when writing a scientific paper, you have to mention the source and say: ICRC books 2005, or 2009, or 2007. And ICRC book doesn't mean anything if there are ten such books or five or six. The Prijedor books of the dead, if there are two, once again I don't know which one she was using. Or maybe she combined the two, but then she would have to say the book from 1998 or the book from 2009. The ICMP has two different reports. Perhaps insignificantly, but they differ. So which one was she using?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So in the example of the ICMP that you just gave, there's a May report, May 2014, then there's a June 2014 update, which she says she used. But you still think she might have meant the May version, the older version. Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's nothing for me to think. In scientific research there is rule, a standard, which says the source is such and such. As soon as I have to think whether Dr. Tabeau was using the one from May or the one from June, then there is something wrong about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Let's go back to your report, D1484 MFI. Here we're going to look at English page 22 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You put to the witness that Dr. Tabeau says she used the June 2014 update. Could you assist me in -- perhaps the witness as well, to tell us where exactly that is found?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: It's on English page 6 of Dr. Tabeau's report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Radovanovic, is -- if an expert says, I used this version of a report, is it your position that in every table that expert witness has to repeat that that's the version, or would one explanation - I used this one - be sufficient unless an exception is specifically made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it's an exception. If it were not an exception, maybe it would be sufficient. But it's not a matter of technique. In scientific reports, you don't do that. You give the source. And here I think it's an exception, as this quotation from the ICMP which Dr. Tabeau explains, that letter is from the month of May, not June. Now, whether the accompanying letter also exists for June, I don't know. But in the report, Dr. Tabeau mentions seven unidentified persons, 15 probably identified, and the ICMP report, I can check, as I have the document, is I believe from May 2014.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm going to move on and return to your report, which is D1484 MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: It's going to be English page 22 and B/C/S page 29, please, and it will be paragraph 67.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: At the very bottom of the English page, you say that: "Without a word of explanation," it continues onto the next page in English. You point out then that the number -- the victims are not numbered sequentially, which you also testified about today. And then at the end of that sentence, you say that they are numbered "in an order known only to the Prosecution expert witness." So here you're referring, in particular, to the first column that's labelled ID in Annex 1 of Dr. Tabeau's report; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Did you read the explanatory notes at the beginning of Dr. Tabeau's annexes?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly which notes you mean. There are several.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'll show you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could we have P7451, which are the four annexes to Dr. Tabeau's report. We're going look at English page 3 and B/C/S page 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in on the text, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We're going to be focusing especially on the bottom of the page. It will be the fourth --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This document not to be shown to the public; I do understand it's under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So I'm going to direct your attention to the bottom of the page, it's the fourth paragraph under the Annex 1 heading. It says: "Parts A and B can be linked with each other through victim names and victim ID. The ID was created by the database software but resembles the order of cases in the original June 2014" - here again we have June 2014 - "ICMP file on DNA identifications of Tomasica victims." So your comment without a word of explanation Dr. Tabeau numbered the individuals this way is not accurate. There is a word of explanation, and it's in the explanatory notes at the beginning of the annexes; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, still, there are known only to Dr. Tabeau. And she says the connection between tables A and B. If you showing the total number of victims and you claim there is a certain number - we don't know - then you don't provide the ID numbers given by ICMP. You derive the number of victims, and how you connect the A and B tables is a matter of your methodology. If you can connect them and give a numerical sequence, then fine. If you cannot compose a numerical sequence, then you provide the ICMP ID numbers. Whether she provides here everything that ICMP has provided or she is making her own table, we don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Did you watch or read the testimony of Dr. Tabeau from the 7th of July, 2015?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date, but I did listen to a lot of it. Whether I've listened to 7 July 2015, is that related to Tomasica?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: It is. Let's see if you remember this part which I'm going to read to you from transcript page 36.771, starting at line 11. The question was: "Q. So, first of all, Dr. Tabeau, the ID. So this is number 162, but we see -- "A. Yes -- "Q. -- that the numbers in this column, the numbers before and after, are not in a successive numeric order, so can you explain that? "A. This reference number, victim number, is the number associated with each victim as reported in the ICMP list from June 2014, the list of identifications." And, again, here you have June 2014. Continuing on: "It was a list that reported jointly on the main cases and reassociations. The Annex 1 exclusively reports on the main cases. Reassociations have been separated, taken out from the list. This is because the whole report I made focuses on individuals, on persons, and not on DNA match reports available in total. So, therefore, we see that the first victim has the number 152, next one 154. So 153 obviously is gone because it was a reassociation, an associated match report." Do you remember that part of Dr. Tabeau's testimony?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So your comment that the victims are numbered "in an order known only to the Prosecution expert witness" is not accurate, is it? She said publicly how she numbered these people.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because, again, it's a manipulation, from my point of view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness -- Witness, whether you like the explanation is a different matter. Whether you call it -- the question was -- you say: She only knows, she never explained. That's more or less what your criticism is. The question by Mr. File simply is: I gave you two places where she explained. Do you agree that she explained how she numbered the lists, the persons? Whether you find it misleading, that's a different matter, but could we focus on what Mr. File asked you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember exactly what's in the first column of the ICMP table, and I don't know whether the ID number is there. But if she copied it from ICMP, then it's probably right. It was not her homework to copy it. It was to provide her own sequence derived from the ICMP. I agree that she copied it from ICMP, Judge Orie. And she and the ICMP know what it means. That's my correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, therefore, we also know how she used the numbering, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you probably know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to another subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Last week, you withdrew part of your critique as a result of basing part of your criticism on an incorrect B/C/S translation of the Tabeau report. And I'm referring to transcript pages 43.626 to 43.627, where you withdraw paragraph 42 of your report and that's where you quoted Dr. Tabeau's report as stating that she used a "DNA matching methodology." And then you pointed out that Dr. Tabeau is not an expert in performing DNA matching. And you withdrew this part of your critique last week because the word "DNA" did not appear in the English original. Do you remember that correction?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I just want to ask you about one additional place where this may have occurred. If we could look again at your report, which is D1484 MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: It's going to be English page 22, B/C/S page 28. Paragraph 65. And I think we need to go to the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So it's this first part that is highlighted in bold, where you claim that in Dr. Tabeau's report she says that 750 shots were fired at a part of the group but 645 shots were fired at the entire group, which is impossible. And I take it you got this figure from the B/C/S translation of Dr. Tabeau's report? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the official B/C/S translation of Dr. Tabeau's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'd like to show P7449, English page 27, B/C/S page 33. It's going to the first paragraph of text in the English version and the only paragraph on the page in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Can you see in the English original it says 570 shots for a part of the group, not 750 shots, and the translation has obviously reversed the numbers. So looking at the numbers now in the English version, would you withdraw this part of your critique?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's part of the illogical. But I still maintain that the number of shots has nothing to do with demography.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a different matter. That's fine. But now knowing that the English version is different from the B/C/S version, do you still stand by your criticism, which, at least Mr. File puts to you, seems to be based on the B/C/S version and not on the English version?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if that translation is incorrect, then my conclusion obviously doesn't stand, if the B/C/S version and the English one have different numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And just for the record, Your Honour, we will submit a revised page for the previous correction as well as this correction so that the B/C/S is accurate in both respects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's a bit alarming, though, that these mistakes are made which produce, then, of course, expert opinions which in themselves may be correct but caused by clerical errors which -- but I leave it to that for the time being. We are looking forward to the revised version of the B/C/S translation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you about your testimony related to corrections of cause of death in Annex 2 of Ewa Tabeau's report. You expressed one of your complaints at transcript page 43.673, starting at line 5. You said: "If Dr. Tabeau did it professionally, she can note that and she can exclude it or she can say, If I have two options, and we're talking about the same case, in how many cases this occurred, and what she did in this case and what she did in another case." Then you is said at transcript page 43.675 to -676 that she should have provided figures for how many corrections she made. And finally, at page 43.677, you questioned Dr. Tabeau's integrity on the basis that she was intentionally hiding something. Do you recall making those points?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I remember saying that, probably in those words which you quote, because I cannot follow the transcript here.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And, for the record, you also made similar arguments in your report at paragraphs 28 and 29. Now my question is: Did you read Annex 2 of Dr. Tabeau's report?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read all of Dr. Tabeau's reports. You have to tell me now exactly what is Annex 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We're going to look at it together.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: It's P7451 - not for broadcast - e-court page English 69, B/C/S 79.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please enlarge it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So this annex is the overview of links between Tomasica main cases and their reassociations. And here on the very first page of Annex 2, you can see the first example of a correction for the individual with ID number 11. On the column furthest to the right, if we can scan over to the right, you have the cause of death determined by the pathologist for different sets of remains, for reassociations to the same person, or the same original main case. Now, in these boxes - and on the B/C/S, the last row is on the next page, page 80 - but four of the five boxes are either blank or unascertained. But the penultimate one, which is at the bottom of the page in B/C/S, that one says "GSI, head," or gun-shot injury to the head. The very final row on this page in the B/C/S and the penultimate row on the page in the English. In the right-hand column, it says "GSI, head." So for all of this person's different sets of reassociated remains, there's an unascertained or blank cause of death except for one of them, which says "GSI, head." Now, if we look over to the left at the cause of death integrated column, which is the fourth column from the left, you can see all of the boxes have been filled in with "GSI, head." So you can see that correction has been made for every set of reassociated remains for that person, taking that one defined cause of death and applying it to all of them; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. First of all, it's difficult for me to follow the entire table, but please pay attention to column 3 at the beginning. It says the main cases and in brackets "Clark plus," and the last column also says Clark. Now, when you see these cause of death integrated, it means that Dr. Tabeau integrated Clark's causes of death, and since the only other causes of death are provided by records of exhumation, here we have integrated records of exhumations, 55 of them, plus Clark. And then the last column also says the Clark report. Does it mean -- and now we are going into the area of what could be but not necessarily. What is in the integrated one, what is in Clark report? If this one is integrated, is it integrated because they are all identical? What she has as the reports of the prosecutor's office of Bosnia-Herzegovina, does it overlap with the Clark report? She states that most of them overlap, but the records made by pathologists, received from the Prosecution, indicate 65, or 70, out of which 55 have known names, or perhaps the number is 50, I don't know off the cuff, and about 15 are unidentified, NN. From this, we cannot see how many corrections Dr. Tabeau made because she doesn't say anywhere, this reference to integrated means 100 per cent overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I think my question was a little more simple than that. It's just that this is an example of a correction because the cause of death determined by Dr. Clark for an individual set of remains, which is shown on the right as unascertained, has become GSI head in the integrated cause of death column. So it's been changed in that column. That's an example of a correction.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau doesn't say that anywhere. She doesn't put in a footnote saying, I corrected this and this. Am I supposed to guess? It has not been presented in an intelligible way. If you are telling me that it's an example of a correction, I don't have to take your word for it. Or Dr. Tabeau's. She has to state it clearly, to show it clearly, through a footnote or in some other way. She is integrating here Clark with Clark and comparing Clark with Clark. Because the number she got from the prosecution is 65. In writing the report she could have put in a footnote and said, I changed 3 or 4, I derived it using computer software. In that case, I wouldn't have had to guess whether it is an example or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But could I ask you: Where the cause of death for some parts of the body found was unascertained, and then later it's said it's an injury to the head, a gun-shot injury to the head, do you have to make a footnote to say, This is something else, or this is a correction? Or does it logically follow that if one body part has an identified cause of death and if that's a part of the body -- of the same body as the other parts which were without a cause of death, should you say in a footnote, This is a correction, or is that obvious from the table itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Dr. Tabeau is not competent enough to correct causes of death. She could have said, I have this case with two causes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the example given is some body parts where apparently the competent expert was unable to tell us what the cause of death was and apparently one set of bodily remains where he could. Now, if the body parts are all of the same person, would a layperson not be able to say, If I take this cause of death which could be established on a certain part of the body, that is, gun-shot injury to the head, if that's a valid one, then it is valid for that person, and, therefore, the other body parts found, which may be legs or arms or whatever, of course, follows the established cause of death for that part of the body for which it could be established. Is there anything wrong with that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From my point of view, yes. Dr. Tabeau could have included a footnote and said, I found an unascertained cause of death and a gun-shot injury to the head. Because maybe in three or five days they would find another bone with another injury, and perhaps not. So in such situations when she needs to decide, she should refer to both documents. Because we have to have in mind that Dr. Clark's documents do not match in the sense of definitions of cause of death with the ones ascertained by the expert from the prosecutor's office of the BiH. So I think professionally she should have said, I'm not going to correct this, I have two reports, one says this and the other one says that, especially as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it true that that is very transparent where at the final column it says unascertained, unascertained, unascertained, gun-shot injury to the head, and that then in the other column she takes it that if there are no two contradicting causes of death, that the unascertained may have been a leg, and, of course, on a leg it's difficult to see whether someone was shot in the head, that she clearly makes -- combines the information, and should she, in addition to that, have considered that if another body part would have been found, which would have shown another cause of death, that that might have changed the correction she made? Do you have to -- then we have to wait for eternity, isn't it, to see whether other body parts would be found.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the methodology that Dr. Tabeau applies anything is possible. She can correct it as a layperson. She can take just one piece of information without correction. She can choose whatever she likes. I don't see a single reason why she would deal with corrections. If this is one and the same person and reassociated remains and the cause of death was established with the reassociated parts, is it then a wish to show as many as possible causes of death that would mean something en masse? If it's a small number, why was it a problem to say, I corrected three or four or five? I don't see the reason why she is making any corrections at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. File -- oh, rather, I would say let's take a break first. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, Ms. Radovanovic. We'll resume at 20 minutes to 2.00. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File, could you tell us whether we're on track as far as time is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I believe we are still on track. I gave the revised estimate of five hours, and I'm doing my best to reduce that where possible. But, so far, I don't think it would extend beyond five hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because, if possible at all, if we could conclude the testimony of this witness tomorrow, that, I think, should be feasible. Mr. Ivetic, I do not know whether you have already a very long list yet or what your estimate would be if things go as they go now?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thus far, I do not have a long list. But again it depends on what develops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you never know. Could the parties try to see to what extent it would be possible to conclude the testimony of this witness by tomorrow so as to avoid that we need another hearing on Wednesday. We take a break and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, again, Your Honours, while we wait for the witness, I can place on the record that, pursuant to your instruction, we did speak, Mr. File and I, during the break, and I was advised that there does not exist a matching log, as mentioned in the last session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Radovanovic, we'll proceed. May I urge you to focus your answers very much on what is asked. Mr. File, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could stay with this document and just go to the next page in both versions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So I'm going to direct your attention to, on the left-hand side, item 31, or ID 31. The B/C/S again carries over to the next page, this time with three additional rows pertaining to the same individual. This is another example of the type of correction we were talking about before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we see item 31 on the English side, please. There are four 31s.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: There are four 31s. All of the integrated cause of death say GSI head and chest. And if we go to the right-hand side, the cause of death is either blank -- starts with blank, the next one is blank, the next one is unascertained, and the final one says GSIs, head and chest.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So I want you to assume for the moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think in the B/C/S we only have part it because I believe that only one of the four is being displayed in the B/C/S. And since the professor doesn't have a hard copy of this, I think it's something she needs to see the next page of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You've now seen the three additional entries under number 31? Please put your question to the witness, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So, Ms. Radovanovic, I want you to assume for the moment that it's obvious that these are corrections. I understand your earlier criticism about how you wanted to see a footnote explaining that. But if you assume that this -- this is obvious these are corrections, this is better than just providing a statistical figure on how many corrections she made; right? You can actually see the corrections with your own eyes and you can count them, if you want. Right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what Dr. Tabeau offers, and I should believe her that this is exactly so. Once again, I tell you, I cannot deal with this because these are integrated lists. As you can see, this is the possibility that three persons -- or, no, two, and whether the unascertained relates to both or to only one, does Dr. Tabeau correct this because she thinks that if she shows more unascertained deaths, that would be more relevant for I don't know what kind of decision. Let me repeat --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please answer the question, whether it's better to present it with the documents rather than to just give a number like five or ten have been corrected, where, as you here can see, what the basis for it is, whether this one were to be preferred above just giving numbers. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's better to provide both. I only assume what Dr. Tabeau did here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Let's go to e-court English page 76 and B/C/S page 87 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We're going to look at the underlying reports for the person with ID number 173. We're not going to use the name in public session. And then I'm going to ask you some questions about them. So, if we could go -- look at the fifth column over, you'll see the site where the first set of remains were exhumed is Jakarina Kosa and the case ID was JK01, or Jakarina Kosa 2001, and body part number 294 BP. And then if we go two columns over to the right, under site name reassociation you see that two additional sets of remains matching this person were found in Tomasica, and then in the column to the right, you have the case ID that ends with the body numbers 326D and 327D. And here you have one cause of death listed as GSI head, and one listed as unascertained.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: If we could look at 65 ter 33793, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm first going to show you the first autopsy report for this person. This is the one from Jakarina Kosa in 2001. It's only in English, but I'll read you to the relevant portions so that you can receive the interpretation. Now, in the upper left corner you can see it says case number JK01/294B. And here, for the record, I would just add that DNA later revealed that there were mixed bones in this collection from two different men so that's why the body number 294B in this autopsy becomes a main case ID of JK01/294BP for person number 173 on our list. The other individual can be found under ID number 49, and his main case ID is JK01/294B-2. So below you have the summary by the forensic medical doctor which says: "Skeletonized and disarticulated incomplete human remains." The next three lines describe the sex and approximate age and height. And then it says: "Several of the bones were fractured, but there were no specific features to these and these may well have been damaged after death. "Since soft tissues are not present, many bones are missing, and present and examined bones show no specific injury, I cannot state the cause of death. "Therefore it should remain unascertained." Now I want to show you the two entries from Clark's report for the reassociations that matched a part of these remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So if we could go to P7444, English page 102 and B/C/S page 108.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So I'm going to start with the second one of these reassociations which is the case 327D. If you look at the general description of the remains in the fifth column, you see that we are talking about bones in and around the left arm and shoulder area. It's the scapula, humerus, and the upper end of the ulna. The next column over to the right says there were no obvious gun-shot injuries. And the final column on the right says the cause of death is unascertained. However, the third set of remains of this person is in the row above with ID 326D.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: In the B/C/S, we need to go to the previous page, 107, where this entry begins. If you look at the general description of remains in the fifth column, you see that we are talking about the skull, C1 to 6 vertebrae and the left clavicle. The next column over says that there was a gun-shot injury to the head causing fragmentation of the skull with an apparent entrance hole at the back on the left side in the occipital region behind the mastoid. And in the B/C/S we need to go to the next page. It says there was an exit at the top of the head. And then in the final column on the right, the cause of death is GSI head, or gun-shot injury to the head, with the minimum number of shots of one from a high-velocity gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So my question for you is: If you have a mixed collection of some of this gentleman's bones with no specific injuries to them, then you have part of his left arm again with no specific injuries, both of them have an unascertained cause of death, finally, you have his head with a bullet-hole in it, and a gun-shot injury cause of death, so if you were going to just for statistical purposes select what was the cause of death for this entire person as opposed to these separate sets of these remains, what would you choose? Unascertained, or gun-shot injury to the head?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A demographer does not do that, nor does he have to do it. He takes the causes of death for which he is certain. But for Dr. Tabeau, what is certain seems not to be adequate. She wants to represent a higher number. So what is unascertained and what she as a demographer would not correct, she would get a smaller number for which she is absolutely certain that the cause of death has been ascertained. So I would exclude this. Possibly I would include a footnote and say there are ten reports with both unascertained and ascertained. So I might point to the fact that it exists, but I'm not the one to establish that this is the one cause of death. I'm not competent for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you how you conclude that she wants to represent a higher number? What's higher here in her approach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is information about both unascertained and ascertained and she says, For the unascertained, if there are some parts available, I said that they are ascertained, that's a wish to show a higher number. She didn't say, I have 100 that are certainly ascertained without any dilemma and another five or ten where a doubt exists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But isn't it true that she presents them as one ascertained cause of death? It's not that she makes three persons having died from gun-shot injuries, but what she says is - at least that's how I understand it - that from what we know, there's one person who died as a result of a gun-shot injury in the head; whereas if she wouldn't have done that, we also would have had one person who died from a gun-shot injury in the head, because that has been established for that skull which was found. So I do not see how she increases the number. It's one in the beginning; it's one in the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In addition, I note that this table gives all three results: One ascertained and two unascertained. So it's for the reader to make -- to choose. Dr. Tabeau is not saying GSI to the head over the two unascertained. She gives you both, all three, and says, That's the result I found.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From what documents, from the integrated Clark and Clark. If Dr. Tabeau is expert enough to add it all up, then that's a different matter. But she's not an expert, and she could have said, I have such and such a number certainly ascertained, and for so many additional cases a report does not exist, and then she could have explained it all. The purpose, when she increases, is to prove that there were many more deaths that are ascertained, than unascertained. I do not know whether that is so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat. She's way too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last part of your answer because you were speaking too fast.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The purpose is to increase the number of those whose death has been ascertained. And Dr. Tabeau draws such a conclusion because she adds the reassociated parts even though this one turns up three times. She doesn't say, I have a number of documents, this is certainly ascertained and these are the injuries, and for these there are various documents, so it's probable or it's likely or it's possible, and then she would view them differently. No. Dr. Tabeau says -- I don't know the exact number but, for example, for 85 per cent the cause of death has been ascertained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But isn't it true that the starting point for Dr. Tabeau is, We know of a person, let's call him A, the cause of death, because gun-shot injury to the head. Now, some other body parts were found of which it was established that they belonged to the same person, and, therefore, we still have at the end one person with unascertained cause of death and that's gun-shot injuries to the head. I have difficulties in understanding on how that adds to numbers, because it's one in the beginning, and, in the end, clearly explained how, she still takes one person, Mr. A, who died as the result of a gun-shot injury to the head. I have difficulties in understanding how that increases the number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't receive interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It increases the number of ascertained causes of death. And, second, I can't follow anymore. Is this the same person where the cause of death is ascertained several times?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's -- it's ascertained once, gun-shot injury in the head. And the other were unascertained. But, Mr. File, please put your next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to a different subject. I'd like to tender number 33793 which was the autopsy report we just looked at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7826, perhaps under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And do we have translations?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do we one report or did we have -- let me see. We had --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We just discussed one report and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One report.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: -- the Clark report is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. Marked for identification pending a translation. Please proceed, Mr. File. Under seal and marked for identification, yes. Please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So to finish today, I would like to shift gears and discuss with you a very simple hypothetical in order to work through a few of the basic principles that we have behind record linkage and data matching. We have a PowerPoint to illustrate this hypothetical which we're going to bring up on Sanction. It's in English, but I'll also be saying everything that's on it and I think it will be obvious to you what's on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we get the 65 ter number so we can follow in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: There is not a -- well, there is a 65 ter number for the final slide, but this is just a demonstrative for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe I'm still entitled to demonstrative exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you like to receive a copy? Perhaps a copy could be made or printed out for Mr. Ivetic who --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So let's say you are teaching a class of five students, and you're going to give them an exam. So you have a registration list from the school for all five students who are registered for your class and it contains the students' first, middle, and last names, and their unique student ID number. So as you can see on this list, the student names and ID numbers that on your list are John Alan Smith, number 121; John Bob Smith, number 122; John Cody Smith, number 123; John Douglas Smith, number 124; and John Elliot Smith, number 125. Now, all five of your students come to your classroom and they take your test, and you recognise them as students who have been taking your class all semester. Now, you told them to put their full names and student ID numbers on the exams, but, unfortunately, when you get the exams back, you see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: If we can go to the next slide.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, for the record, this does comport to what has been given to us as 33804. And I just checked on web mail, I have not received a copy of any PowerPoint presentations to be used in court. So, again, I don't know at this point what we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File, is there any way that we could perhaps print out or --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Yes, we can print out a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then, please, with all the elements of the PowerPoint presentation. Now, Mr. Ivetic, whether it's PowerPoint or whether it's a sheet or whatever is not, I think, decisive, it's just a way of putting it on the screen. That's what PowerPoint is for.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. And with other PowerPoint presentations, it's customary as we have received, I think with Dr. Tabeau, slides. You have slides in PowerPoint and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- each slide is a different presentation of data. And as I read 33804, it is one sheet of paper that is not resembling exactly what is on the screen we have right now, so I'm missing -- I have -- I might have the final slide, but I'm missing all the other slides. And I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know -- let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- if something is being used with the witness, I'm entitled to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic. Mr. File, are there other -- okay, there we see -- could you make a printout, which is possible in PowerPoint, to make a printout of the whole of all the slides so that Mr. Ivetic receives them right away, all of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We certainly can. He has just received a preview essentially of the final slide but that's -- we can print out all of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if you want to show more, then I think it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: It's no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it's right that Mr. Ivetic received disclosure of all the slides you want to present. You'll receive them in a second, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So if we go to the next slide, you'll see what you receive on the exams that come back from your students, unfortunately. The first one just writes J and 126, so you have one person who just put a single initial and a clearly wrong student ID --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File, you are saying that it's a wrong ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: In the sense that it doesn't match any of the five IDs on the list --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether the first one gives the wrong ID or whether the student gives the wrong IDs, we do not know yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: The next person puts Jack Smith, 22, so someone else may have used a nickname, forgot to put middle name, and put a wrong or incomplete student ID. The next one is John, 121. So there you have someone who put their first name and student ID, it appears. The next one says Codee, spelled with two es. So here you may have put only their middle name and may have misspelled their own name, or perhaps it's misspelled on your registration list. And the last one appears to be the model student who puts John Douglas Smith, 124, with all four fields filled out. You don't have any additional information, such as handwriting or other things, to try to decide who to assign these exams to. So if you are faced with a situation like this, figuring out who wrote what exam is fundamentally a matching exercise; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hypothetically speaking, yes; but scientifically speaking, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We are --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you take it as a simplified example, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: That's exactly what we are doing. In this sort of circumstance, you would want to start with a more restrictive set of criteria such as an exact match of the first name, the middle name, the last name, and the ID number. And if we can go to the next slide, it would give you one match, this one where it matches identically; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So I want to take you through a series of additional less restrictive matching criteria. The next one, if you used first name and ID number, you could get another match of John Alan Smith, 121, to John, 121. If we can go to the next one. If you used a fuzzy search for the middle name, which is like if you did a search for matching the first three letters of the middle name, for example, you could get another match of John Cody Smith, 123, to Codee. If we go to the next. If you use the first initial and the last name and the fuzzy ID, you could get another match between John Bob Smith, 122, to Jack Smith, 22. That would be as if you matched only the last two digits of the ID. And then for the last person, you could use first initial only, but you could make that match since there's now only one person left in your class with that first initial. So John Elliot Smith, 125, could match with J. 126. So my first question is: Just looking at this hypothetical example, and, of course, it's a simplified hypothetical, you would agree that this probably the right result in terms of making the best possible matches between the exams and the students; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have an accurate ID, yes. If you don't have an ID or you have an inaccurate ID, then no. You are giving me examples with correct ID numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I maintain that in many sources of information used by Dr. Tabeau, there are no ID numbers or there is an insufficient number of accurate IDs.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: For now, we're just talking about this example. We're not talking about Dr. Tabeau's sources. But in this case, this is the best possible match for these exams and students; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a correct ID, such a simple case would not be a problem. But this is an extremely simplified case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- isn't a good last answer for the day, that this is a simplified, extremely simplified case. We leave it to that. I instruct you again that you should not speak or communicate in any way with whomever about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning. And we will try to do our utmost best to see whether we can conclude hearing your testimony tomorrow, but this is not a guarantee. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 3rd of May, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.
